reference_frames.terrain: MOON_ME tied to JPL DE421, spherical radius 1737.4 km
reference_frames.frame_alignment_note: PGDA terrain is explicitly MOON_ME/DE421. Horizons uses the lunar Mean-Earth DE421 frame for lunar topocentric sites, while local SPICE explicitly resolves MOON_ME_DE440_ME421, which NAIF defines as closely aligned with DE421 Mean-Earth. Horizons target ephemerides are DE441 and the compact local SPK is DE440s.

local_topocentric.up: normal to 1737.4 km lunar reference sphere
local_topocentric.azimuth: clockwise from north: N=0, E=90, S=180, W=270
local_topocentric.elevation: angle above plane perpendicular to local Up

assumptions.terrain_occlusion: Each apparent disk is intersected by a locally straight skyline at the object's center azimuth.
assumptions.earth_disk: Horizons equatorial angular diameter is treated as a circular disk; oblateness and limb position angle are omitted.
assumptions.sun_disk: Uniform circular disk; limb darkening is omitted.
assumptions.dte: Geometric line of sight only; no antenna, link budget, Earth ground-station, or operational constraints.

comms_potential.rule: Earth center clearance <= 0 degrees: index 0; otherwise Earth absolute elevation <= 2 degrees: index 30; otherwise index 100. The percentages are display categories, not RF signal strength or link reliability.
comms_potential.disk_visibility_distinction: Existing geometric DTE windows count any exposed Earth disk. The center-based index can be zero while an Earth limb remains visible.

assumptions.window_detection: left-closed sample-grid intervals; each state applies from its timestamp to the next timestamp, so transition timing precision is bounded by the configured step

omissions: lander self-shadowing and panel thermal behavior
power_model.scenario_status: illustrative panel pointing geometry; not a measured or flight-qualified lander electrical subsystem

fixed_vertical_north.description: Fixed vertical collecting face; outward normal points north.

fixed_tilt_80_north.description: Fixed face tilted 80 degrees from horizontal toward north.

limited_gimbal.description: Ideal two-axis mount limited to 0-80 degree tilt and north +/-90 degree yaw.

metadata.interpolation: maximum apparent elevation across the 10 m local and 240 m outer spherical-geodesic raycasts; periodic linear interpolation
metadata.curvature_model: spherical chord geometry in both scales

metadata.selection_method: Exact original rays at integer azimuths; no azimuth interpolation or second DEM raycast
metadata.minimum_clearance_definition: Point-source center elevation above the local tangent plane required to clear the LOLA terrain skyline

windows.method: left-closed sample-grid intervals; each state applies from its timestamp to the next timestamp, so transition timing precision is bounded by the configured step

sun.independent_position_validation_note: This block checks the operational Horizons response for parser, cadence, range, angle-bound, and disk-size consistency. Independent position errors are reported separately under validation.independent_spice.

published_psr_crosscheck.interpretation: PGDA classifies this site as NOT_PSR and the simulation finds direct sunlight, so broad behavior is consistent.
published_psr_crosscheck.scope: broad categorical check only; the PGDA PSR product is not a time-matched illumination time series

independent_spice.scope: Independent local implementation cross-check of target-center azimuth, elevation, apparent range, and angular diameter at all requested epochs
limitations: Horizons uses DE441 while the compact local SPK is DE440s; the comparison intentionally spans those closely related JPL ephemeris releases.
CSPICE CN+S includes converged light time and stellar aberration but not the relativistic light deflection included in Horizons apparent observer quantities.
SPICE validates celestial center geometry only; LOLA terrain occultation remains a separate local calculation.
Horizons remains the operational ephemeris source; local SPICE is an independent implementation cross-check and is not averaged into the displayed trajectory.
NASA PGDA PSR provides a broad categorical check, not a time-matched quantitative illumination comparison.
